titre: External power supply or USB-C charger sold in France: what the seller must hold before the product is made available
perimetre: A mains-powered external power supply or USB-C charger (AC input, DC output, no radio function, no battery) placed or made available on the market in France, resold under the original brand or sold under the seller's own brand, alone or supplied with another device; the file lists the documents, markings and information each role must hold or check, and never states that a product complies.

criteres.question: Under which brand do you sell the charger?

valeurs.libelle: Under my own name or trade mark
Unchanged, under the original brand of the company that made it

criteres.aide: Look at the name printed on the product and its packaging: is it yours or the original maker's?

criteres.question: Where is your company established?

valeurs.libelle: In another Member State of the European Union

criteres.aide: The country of the registered office of the company that sells.

criteres.question: Has another company established in the EU already placed this product on the EU market before it reaches you?
criteres.aide: Yes if you buy it from an EU manufacturer, importer or wholesaler; no if you bring it in yourself from a supplier outside the EU.

criteres.question: Is the supplier you buy the product from established in France?
criteres.aide: No if the product comes to you from another Member State or from outside the EU.

criteres.question: Do you offer the product online or by another means of distance selling to buyers in France?
criteres.aide: Web shop, marketplace listing, mail order, phone order.

criteres.question: Is the offer addressed to consumers?
criteres.aide: Yes if private individuals can buy it, no if you sell only to businesses.

criteres.question: Is the charger sold alone or supplied with another device?

valeurs.libelle: Supplied with a radio device of one of these kinds: handheld mobile phone, tablet, digital camera, headphones, headset, handheld videogame console, portable speaker, e-reader, keyboard, mouse, portable navigation system, earbuds, laptop
Supplied with another kind of device

criteres.aide: A device has a radio function when it uses, for example, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth or a mobile network.

criteres.question: When are the units first supplied on the EU market?
criteres.aide: The date of the first supply of each unit on the EU market, not the date of your own resale.

criteres.question: What input voltage is the product rated for?

valeurs.libelle: Alternating current between 50 V and 1 000 V (for example 100-240 V AC mains)
Direct current between 75 V and 1 500 V
Below 50 V AC and below 75 V DC
Above 1 000 V AC or above 1 500 V DC

criteres.aide: Read the INPUT line of the rating label.

criteres.question: Does the product convert the mains AC input into one or more lower voltage DC or AC outputs?
criteres.aide: Compare the INPUT and OUTPUT lines of the rating label (for example input 100-240 V AC, output 5 V to 20 V DC).

criteres.question: What is the nameplate output power?
criteres.aide: Read the output power in watts on the rating label or the datasheet.

criteres.question: Is the power supply in a physical enclosure separate from the device it powers, connected to it by a cable or connector?
criteres.aide: Yes for a wall charger or a power brick; no for a power supply built inside the device.

criteres.question: What kind of equipment is the charger meant to power?

valeurs.libelle: Information technology equipment intended primarily for use in the domestic environment

criteres.aide: Leave unanswered if neither applies: only point 2 of Annex I to Regulation (EU) 2019/1782 is in the source texts, the other kinds of household and office equipment are not.

criteres.question: Does the product intentionally emit or receive radio waves to communicate?
criteres.aide: For example Wi-Fi or Bluetooth listed on the datasheet. A plain mains charger has none.

roles.pourquoi: You sell the charger under your own name or trade mark: a person who has equipment designed or manufactured and markets it under his name or trade mark is the manufacturer, and an importer or distributor who places equipment on the market under his name or trade mark is considered a manufacturer and takes on the manufacturer obligations.

You are established within the Union, you keep the original brand and nobody in the Union has placed the product on the market before you: you make the first supply on the Union market of equipment coming from a third country, which is what the definition of importer describes.

You resell under the original brand a product that another company has already placed on the Union market: you are a person in the supply chain, other than the manufacturer or the importer, who makes the equipment available on the market.

exigences.titre: Electrical safety file, CE marking and identification on the product

acte.nom: Directive 2014/35/EU (electrical equipment designed for use within certain voltage limits)

exigences.pourquoi: The charger is rated for an input within the range the Directive covers (between 50 and 1 000 V AC, or between 75 and 1 500 V DC); it has no radio function, so the rule that takes radio equipment out of this Directive does not come into play. Annex II lists the equipment left outside the scope: check that the product is none of it.

exigences.titre: Electromagnetic compatibility file and CE marking
exigences.pourquoi: The Directive applies to equipment, which includes any apparatus: a finished appliance made available as a single functional unit, intended for the end-user and liable to generate electromagnetic disturbance or to be affected by it. A mains charger sold to end-users is a finished appliance of that kind, and with no radio function it is not radio equipment as defined in Directive 2014/53/EU.

exigences.titre: Ecodesign of the external power supply: efficiency file, EC declaration, nameplate and manual information

acte.nom: Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/1782 (ecodesign requirements for external power supplies)

exigences.pourquoi: The product meets the facts of the definition of an external power supply: it converts mains AC input into a lower voltage output, sits in an enclosure separate from the device it powers, has a nameplate output power not exceeding 250 W and is used with information technology equipment for the domestic environment. The Regulation applies from 1 April 2020 and is repealed with effect from 14 December 2028; the articles of Directive 2009/125/EC on CE marking, declaration and importer duties still apply to products covered by such an implementing measure. Check that the product is none of the exclusions of Article 1(2). A unit placed on the market between 14 December 2025 and 14 December 2028 that meets Regulation (EU) 2025/2052 is considered to comply.

obligations.resume: The manufacturer must compile a technical documentation file making it possible to assess conformity with the implementing measure, including a general description of the product and its intended use, the standards applied and the results of the measurements carried out on the ecodesign requirements.
obligations.qui_agit: The manufacturer compiles the file, with the measurement results compared with the ecodesign requirements.

preuves.libelle: Technical documentation file for ecodesign (Directive 2009/125/EC, Annex IV, point 2, with the declared values of Regulation (EU) 2019/1782, Annex II, point 2(c))

obligations.resume: For the conformity assessment, the technical documentation shall contain the declared values of the parameters listed in Annex II, point 2(c).
obligations.qui_agit: The provision states what the file must contain and names no person; it is listed for the manufacturer because Annex IV to Directive 2009/125/EC gives the manufacturer the task of compiling that file.

preuves.libelle: Technical documentation file for ecodesign (Directive 2009/125/EC, Annex IV, point 2, with the declared values of Regulation (EU) 2019/1782, Annex II, point 2(c))

obligations.resume: Before the product is placed on the market, a CE marking shall be affixed and an EC declaration of conformity issued, by which the manufacturer or its authorised representative ensures and declares that the product complies with all relevant provisions of the implementing measure.
obligations.qui_agit: The manufacturer, or its authorised representative, issues the declaration and has the CE marking affixed before placing on the market.

preuves.libelle: EC declaration of conformity referring to Regulation (EU) 2019/1782, with the elements of Annex VI to Directive 2009/125/EC
CE marking on the product or its data plate

obligations.resume: The EC declaration of conformity shall contain the elements specified in Annex VI and shall refer to the appropriate implementing measure.
obligations.qui_agit: The provision states what the declaration must contain; it is listed for the manufacturer, who issues the declaration under Article 5(1).

preuves.libelle: EC declaration of conformity referring to Regulation (EU) 2019/1782, with the elements of Annex VI to Directive 2009/125/EC

obligations.resume: The manufacturer or its authorised representative shall keep the documents relating to the conformity assessment and the declarations of conformity available for inspection for 10 years after the last of the product has been manufactured, and make them available within 10 days of a request.
obligations.qui_agit: The manufacturer, or its authorised representative, keeps the documents and hands them over within 10 days when asked.

preuves.libelle: Ecodesign information on the nameplate (Regulation (EU) 2019/1782, Annex II, point 2(a))

obligations.resume: From 1 April 2020, instruction manuals for end-users (where applicable) and free access websites of manufacturers, importers or authorised representatives shall include the information listed in Annex II, point 2(b), in the order set out.
obligations.qui_agit: The manual and the free access website of the manufacturer, the importer or the authorised representative carry the information. The list of items is not in the source texts.

exigences.titre: Waste equipment (WEEE): producer because you sell in France under your own brand

acte.nom: Directive 2012/19/EU on waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE)

exigences.pourquoi: The charger is electrical and electronic equipment, and from 15 August 2018 the Directive covers all such equipment. You are established in France and market or resell the equipment there under your own name or trade mark, which is the first or second case of the definition of producer.

obligations.resume: Member States shall ensure that producers mark the equipment placed on the market with the crossed-out wheeled bin symbol of Annex IX; only in exceptional cases, because of the size or function of the product, is the symbol printed on the packaging, the instructions for use and the warranty.
obligations.qui_agit: The producer marks the equipment with the symbol; the Directive is addressed to Member States, so the binding wording for France is in French law, which is not in the source texts.

preuves.libelle: Crossed-out wheeled bin symbol on the product (Directive 2012/19/EU, Annex IX)

obligations.resume: Member States shall ensure that each producer, or its authorised representative where one is appointed, is registered as required and can enter in the national register the information reflecting its activities in that Member State.
obligations.qui_agit: The producer (or its authorised representative) registers in the national register of producers; the French register and its procedure are not in the source texts.

preuves.libelle: Proof of registration in the national register of producers of electrical and electronic equipment

obligations.resume: Member States shall ensure that producers provide at least for the financing of the collection, treatment, recovery and environmentally sound disposal of WEEE from private households deposited at collection facilities.
obligations.qui_agit: The producer provides for that financing; how this is organised in France is not in the source texts.

preuves.libelle: Proof that the financing of collection, treatment, recovery and disposal of household WEEE is provided for

exigences.titre: Economic operator established in the Union: tasks and contact details

acte.nom: Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 on market surveillance and compliance of products

exigences.pourquoi: The charger is subject to Directives listed in Article 4(5) (among them 2011/65/EU, 2014/30/EU, 2014/35/EU and 2009/125/EC), so it may be placed on the market only if an economic operator established in the Union is responsible for the tasks of Article 4(3). You are established in the Union: a manufacturer established in the Union is that operator, and so is an importer when the manufacturer is not established in the Union. The Article applies from 16 July 2021.

obligations.resume: The economic operator shall verify that the EU declaration of conformity and the technical documentation have been drawn up, keep the declaration at the disposal of the market surveillance authorities, ensure the technical documentation can be made available on request, provide information on a reasoned request, report risks and cooperate on corrective action.
obligations.qui_agit: The economic operator referred to in Article 4(1) performs these tasks; Article 4(2) says who that is.

preuves.libelle: EU declaration of conformity (one declaration naming every Union act that requires one)
Technical documentation of the manufacturer, obtainable on request for the market surveillance authorities

obligations.resume: The name, registered trade name or registered trade mark and the contact details, including the postal address, of the economic operator shall be indicated on the product or on its packaging, the parcel or an accompanying document.
obligations.qui_agit: The provision names no person; it requires the operator's details to appear, and it is listed for the manufacturer and the importer because they are the sellers who can be that operator under Article 4(2).

preuves.libelle: Name and contact details, including postal address, of the economic operator established in the Union, on the product, its packaging, the parcel or an accompanying document

exigences.titre: Economic operator established in the Union: to be found, because the manufacturer is outside the Union

acte.nom: Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 on market surveillance and compliance of products

exigences.pourquoi: The charger is subject to Directives listed in Article 4(5), so it may be placed on the market only if an economic operator established in the Union is responsible for the tasks of Article 4(3). You sell under your own brand from outside the Union, so you are not a manufacturer established in the Union: the operator has to be an importer, an authorised representative with a written mandate or, failing those, a fulfilment service provider established in the Union. The Article applies from 16 July 2021, and an online offer directed at a Member State counts as making available on the market.

obligations.resume: The economic operator is a manufacturer established in the Union, an importer where the manufacturer is not established in the Union, an authorised representative with a written mandate from the manufacturer for the Article 4(3) tasks, or a fulfilment service provider established in the Union for the products it handles where none of the others is established in the Union.
obligations.qui_agit: The provision lists who can be the operator. Where it is an authorised representative, the written mandate comes from the manufacturer.

preuves.libelle: Identification of the economic operator established in the Union for this product (importer, authorised representative with its written mandate, or fulfilment service provider)

obligations.resume: The name, registered trade name or registered trade mark and the contact details, including the postal address, of the economic operator shall be indicated on the product or on its packaging, the parcel or an accompanying document.
obligations.qui_agit: The provision names no person; it is listed for the manufacturer, whose product, packaging or parcel has to carry the details of the operator established in the Union.

preuves.libelle: Name and contact details, including postal address, of the economic operator established in the Union, on the product, its packaging, the parcel or an accompanying document

exigences.titre: Online offer to consumers: information that must appear in the listing
exigences.pourquoi: You offer the product online or by another means of distance selling to consumers, so it is deemed to be made available on the market. For a product subject to Union harmonisation legislation, Article 2(1) sets aside Chapter II for the risks already covered and Chapter III, Section 1 entirely; Article 19 on the content of distance offers is not in the parts set aside. The Regulation applies from 13 December 2024.

obligations.resume: Where economic operators make products available online or through other means of distance sales, the offer shall clearly and visibly indicate the manufacturer's name and postal and electronic address, the responsible person where the manufacturer is not established in the Union, information identifying the product including a picture, and any warning or safety information in a language easily understood by consumers, as determined by the Member State.
obligations.qui_agit: The economic operator that publishes the distance offer puts this information in the offer.

preuves.libelle: In the online offer: manufacturer name, registered trade name or trade mark, postal and electronic address
In the online offer, where the manufacturer is not established in the Union: name, postal and electronic address of the responsible person
In the online offer: picture of the product, its type and any other product identifier
In the online offer: the warnings and safety information of the product, in the language determined by the Member State

exigences.titre: Charger supplied with a phone, tablet, laptop or similar radio device: offer without charger and pictogram

acte.nom: Directive 2014/53/EU (radio equipment), as amended by Directive (EU) 2022/2380

exigences.pourquoi: The charger itself is not radio equipment, but it is supplied with radio equipment of a category listed in Annex Ia, Part I. The duties below attach to the offer of that radio equipment together with a charging device. Member States apply these rules from 28 December 2024 for points 1.1 to 1.12 of the list and from 28 April 2026 for laptops.

obligations.resume: Where an economic operator offers consumers and other end-users the possibility to acquire the radio equipment together with a charging device, it shall also offer them the possibility of acquiring that radio equipment without any charging device.
obligations.qui_agit: The economic operator that offers the bundle also offers the radio equipment without a charging device.

preuves.libelle: Offer of the same radio equipment without any charging device

obligations.resume: Economic operators shall ensure that the information on whether a charging device is included is shown by the pictogram of Annex Ia, Part III, printed on the packaging or affixed to it as a sticker, displayed visibly and legibly and, in distance selling, close to the price indication.
obligations.qui_agit: The economic operators ensure that the pictogram is on the packaging and, for distance selling, next to the price.

preuves.libelle: Pictogram on the packaging showing whether a charging device is included (Directive 2014/53/EU, Annex Ia, Part III)

lacunes: French language requirement for instructions and safety information (loi 94-665, Article 2): text not obtained. The entries only say "the language determined by the Member State".

French WEEE rules (Code de l'environnement: registration, eco-organisation, unique identifier, Triman and sorting information): texts not obtained. Only the Directive, addressed to Member States, is cited.
French transposition of Directives 2014/35/EU, 2014/30/EU, 2011/65/EU and 2014/53/EU: not downloaded. The Directives are cited.

Directive 2014/30/EU, Article 2(2)(a) (exclusion of radio equipment) is not in the source texts. The file covers products without a radio function; for a product with one, the electromagnetic compatibility entry returns "not applicable" without a cited basis and the radio equipment duties are not written.
Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 (batteries): no provision in the source texts, so no battery criterion and no battery requirement. To be reopened if the product contains or ships with a battery.

Regulation (EU) 2019/1782: the lists of nameplate items (Annex II, 2(a)), manual and website items (2(b)) and declared values (2(c)) are quoted by their introductory words only; Annex I is limited to point 2 (information technology equipment). The exclusions of Article 1(2) are cited but not turned into criteria.
Regulation (EU) 2025/2052 (applicable from 14 December 2028): its requirements are not in the source texts, so a unit placed on the market on or after that date gets no ecodesign work list.
Low Voltage Directive, Annex II (equipment outside the scope) is cited but not turned into a criterion.
Modification of a product already placed on the market (Article 10 of Directive 2014/35/EU and equivalents): not turned into a criterion; only the own-brand case makes the seller a manufacturer here.

A reseller established outside the Union that keeps the original brand and brings the product to the Union market itself matches no role: the importer must be established within the Union. No work list is produced by role in that case.

Whether the manufacturer of an imported product is established in the Union is not asked; the importer duties under Article 4 of Directive 2009/125/EC and Article 4(2)(b) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 depend on it and say so in their wording.

Directive 2014/35/EU, Article 6(4) and 6(8), Article 8(5) to 8(7) and Article 9(3) onwards (sample testing, corrective action, storage and transport, cooperation), Directive 2014/30/EU Articles 7(5) and 18, Directive 2011/65/EU Article 7(b), (e), (f), (g): not in the source texts, no entry.

Regulation (EU) 2023/988, Article 20(3) (importers and distributors inform the manufacturer of an accident) is in the source texts but produces no document or marking: not listed as a requirement. The definition of "product" (Article 3(1)) is not in the source texts.
Regulation (EC) No 765/2008, Article 30 (general principles of the CE marking), harmonised standards, REACH, POPs, packaging, energy labelling and customs formalities: not examined.

The EC declaration of conformity under Directive 2009/125/EC is kept as a separate evidence item: no source text states that it may be merged into the single EU declaration of Article 15(3) of Directive 2014/35/EU.
